trigger: Step species "ext": proof head in _EXT_HEADS (funext, Set.ext, Subtype.ext, propext...) or a name ending .ext (helpers.py:175 _read_justification); step.premises empty
typed_info: the ext lemma's name (dropped: _read_justification returns "" as the head) and its argument: the pointwise / memberwise fact under the binder (a lambda whose body is the per-x equality or iff)
why: the per-point fact is in the term and not stated; a form would read "since f(x) = g(x) for every x" / "both sets have the same elements"

trigger: as above with step.premises non-empty
typed_info: as above, plus the cited premises
why: cites the fact the pointwise step uses; still names the method, not the per-point identity, but it points to the fact on the page

trigger: a rewrite_chain / rewrite_pieces row whose reason lemma (row.reason.declaration) has reading "algebra" in data/.../rewrite-readings.json (108 of the file's lemma entries: mul_comm, add_assoc, sub_eq_add_neg, ...) — the data marker _DATA_ALGEBRA
typed_info: the rewrite lemma's name and its instantiated statement; row.before / row.after (typed exprs), the rewrite_side
count_method: page: "\text{algebra}" in align rows; "by algebra" in sentences
why: the lemma used is in hand and "algebra" names none; a form can name the identity class from the lemma (commutativity, distributivity, ...) or show the identity instance

trigger: a congruence-wrapper row whose inner head is a composition-normalization head (composition-normalization.json) and has no reading of its own
typed_info: the inner head constant and the wrapper's function
why: same as above: the head is in hand, "algebra" names nothing

trigger: a constructed row from a `simpa using h` meeting: the lemma's statement to the goal's statement, composing two simp runs (row built with reason="algebra", premise_steps=())
typed_info: the two simp runs (first, second) and their rewrite lemmas; goal_before_tex/goal_after_tex
why: a row made by the walk with a hard-coded label; the simp lemmas of both runs are available

phrase: Hence X — by simplification / integer arithmetic / linear arithmetic / ring normalisation / positivity / function-property automation ... (final closer)
trigger: the theorem's final closer: step.name = closing_phrase = _TACTIC_PHRASE of the LAST tactic line in the Lean SOURCE text that has a phrase (a text scan of Main.lean, not the term); per-arm variant at render.py:396-403 (seg_phrase)
typed_info: the closer's term (its head and certificate lemmas), the tactic line actually closing the goal, and the premises
count_method: page: "Hence ... — by <tactic phrase>." (598 of all 1226 "— by <tactic>." are simplification)
why: the reason is read from source text, the last automation line anywhere in the proof, not the step that closes; nothing typed ties the phrase to this goal

trigger: closer, no rewrite_chain, proof_head == "tactic"; phrase from step.proof_head_phrase via _TACTIC_PHRASE (render.py:21); empty phrase -> "direct computation" (render.py:3321)
typed_info: the tactic name (proof_head_phrase) and the term it produced; for linarith/omega the hypotheses combined
why: names the procedure as the argument; the facts it combines are not cited

trigger: Step species "computation": head in _DECIDE_HEADS (of_decide_eq_true, decide...) or in a tactic namespace (Mathlib.Tactic.*, Mathlib.Meta.NormNum.*, Mathlib.Meta.Positivity.*, Linarith.*, Nat.Linear.*, Int.Linear.*)
typed_info: the head constant c (dropped: returned as ""), which identifies the tactic (ring certificate, norm_num isNat, linarith proof, positivity) and the instantiated goal
why: the certificate's head tells which tactic ran and is discarded; for decide/norm_num the evaluated numerals are in the goal

phrase: A contradiction follows by integer arithmetic. / By integer arithmetic, this contradicts (n). / Hence X by integer arithmetic / computation / contradiction.
trigger: closer with step.auxiliary_proof_class in O (omega), R, B
typed_info: the omega/decide term, step.premises
why: with premises it cites them (closer to a form); without, it is a procedure name only

trigger: Step species "instance": head in _INSTANCE_HEADS (inferInstance, inferInstanceAs, instDecidableEqNat, Classical.propDecidable) (helpers.py:181)
typed_info: the instance's type (the class applied to its arguments) and the instance constant found
why: typeclass inference is Lean vocabulary; the instance found (e.g. ℝ is a complete space) is the reason

trigger: closer whose head is inferInstance (_other_head_reading "standard")
typed_info: the instance type and constant
why: as above

trigger: Step species "field": head in _FIELD_HEADS (Subtype.property, Fin.isLt, Set.Elem.property, ...) (helpers.py:177)
typed_info: the object z and its type (z : S, i : Fin n): the membership or bound the field states
why: its type is Lean's view; a form says "since z ∈ S" / "since i < n, i being an index below n"

trigger: Step species "nonempty": head in _NONEMPTY_HEADS (Nonempty.intro, nonempty_of_exists, Nonempty.map) (helpers.py:179)
typed_info: the element: Nonempty.intro's explicit argument (a term, renderable)
why: says an element exists without naming the element the term gives

phrase: Applying the same function to both sides of (n) gives X.
trigger: species "restate" with congruence_eval mode "arg" whose function tex is empty (congrArg's function did not render)
typed_info: congrArg's function argument (expr), the cited Eq premise
count_method: page: "Applying the same function to both sides of"
why: the function is in the term; "the same function" names nothing

phrase: This follows by applying the same function to both sides of (n).
trigger: a sufficiency closure of kind "congruence" (Q523) whose reduced goal is the chain's endpoint
typed_info: congrArg's function and the cited premises
why: the function is deliberately unnamed (Q523)

trigger: a closer whose goal == tex (restates) with no why, no step.name, no apm_claim_reason (_claim_reason_suffix empty) and no premises; also 3941 (Subtype.mk / withheld witness), 3986 (projection, no cited), 4074 (species witness)
typed_info: step.proof_head_name and its arguments (the closing term), any premise steps the term uses
why: no reason at all; the closing term's head is typed and not read

phrase: In either case, the claim holds.
trigger: closer species "cases" (Or.elim / dite / two-arm casesOn) whose goal == tex
typed_info: the split's scrutinee and both arms' closers (already printed above it)
rule: D3 (if the alternatives are not stated)
why: a standard case-split conclusion when each arm is printed and names its alternative; a gap only where the arms are not on the page (D3 decides, not this site)

phrase: In either case, X. / In all three/n cases, the claim holds.
trigger: closer species cases / cases_three / cases_many
typed_info: as above
why: as above

phrase: X, which is immediate. / which is immediate from (n)
trigger: Step species "trivial": head in _TRIVIAL_HEADS (le_refl, le_rfl, trivial, True.intro, Set.mem_univ, le_top, bot_le, zero_le, ...)
typed_info: the head constant (which says why: reflexivity, x ∈ univ, ⊥ ≤ x, 0 ≤ n)
count_method: page: "which is immediate." / "which is immediate from"
why: immediate hides a named fact (le_refl, zero_le...) that a form can state: "since 0 ≤ n for every natural n"

trigger: species "elementary_fact" with empty step.phrase
typed_info: the elementary-factor lemma (elementary-factors.json key) whose phrase was not found
why: the lemma is known; its phrase is missing

trigger: have/let with no why, no block, no premises (Q139: "its term applies a library fact directly"); or species restate with no premises (4171); or fact_why empty at 3905
typed_info: the library fact the term applies (its head constant / justified_by when not cited), the instantiation
count_method: page: "We have \(..\)." with nothing after (includes all three lines)
why: the applied library fact is in the term and not named (Q139 counted 3557 such sentences)

phrase: Hence X, the hypotheses being contradictory.
trigger: closer species "contradiction" with no step.refutes
typed_info: the two conflicting facts (the by_contra supposition and the fact refuting it) as premise steps
why: does not say which facts conflict; Q526's refutes-form covers the case where the supposition is typed

phrase: The hypotheses are contradictory, so the claim holds. / This case is impossible.
trigger: closer with proof_head == "contra", no cited
typed_info: absurd/False.elim's argument (the False proof) and its premises
why: as above when nothing is cited

phrase: A contradiction follows by <tactic>. / This is a contradiction.
trigger: a closer of False with no premise cited; reason from step.phrase or _TACTIC_PHRASE[step.name]
typed_info: the refuting term and the facts it combines
why: procedure name or nothing

trigger: species "contradiction" (by_contra head) on a have/part
typed_info: the supposition (negated fact) and the refuting step inside
why: the supposition is not stated (D3: "a proof by contradiction states its supposition")

trigger: species "induction" (.rec / brecOn / strongRec heads)
typed_info: the recursor, motive, and the base and step terms
why: names the method; base and step cases are not printed

trigger: closer whose head is eq_self / of_eq_true / not_false_eq_true / *._simp_1 (_other_head_reading "simplification")
typed_info: the simp lemma constant (the ._simp_1 name) and the goal
why: the head names the simp lemma that closed it; "simplification" names the procedure

trigger: closer whose head is Mathlib.Meta.NormNum.isNat_*
typed_info: the evaluated numerals in the goal
why: a computation presented as the reason; the numerals evaluated are in hand

phrase: Hence X, both sides being equal.
trigger: closer head le_refl / le_rfl (order_reflexive) after a normalising tactic
typed_info: the normalised goal (sides equal after rw/simp) and the rewrites that made it so
why: the printed sides can differ (Q61); the normalisation that equates them is not shown

trigger: closer proof_head == "refl" (rfl / Eq.refl), no rewrite chain
typed_info: the constants that must be unfolded for the sides to agree (delta reduction of the goal)
why: by definition without naming the definition; the unfolded constant is computable from the goal

trigger: closer proof_head_detail match/casesOn, not neutral
typed_info: the scrutinee and the arms
why: the cases are not named

trigger: dite closer whose condition did not render (seqsplit/texttt)
typed_info: the dite condition expr
why: the condition is typed but unprinted

phrase: It suffices to show X, by <tactic phrase>.
trigger: species "paper_tactic": a rewrite chain of only generated tactic normal forms; step.phrase from the tactic
typed_info: the tactic's rewrite lemmas (the chain rows it replaced)
count_method: page: "It suffices to show \( .. \), by / using / since"
why: the tactic name stands in for the rewrites; the rows are typed and were dropped as normal forms

phrase: Define a = v (v a literal, or an existing object)
trigger: Step kind "define" (let / set) whose value is a numeral (OfNat literal), an anonymous constructor of a literal (⟨2, _⟩ : ℝ≥0), a coercion, or a bare existing local
typed_info: the let value expr (is it a literal / coercion / fvar), the let type
why: a name for a literal or for an object that already has one; a form either substitutes or states the type it changes ("let γ = 2 as a nonnegative real")

phrase: Definition card "lhs = rhs" where lhs prints as the body (A = A)
trigger: a definition whose head has a display rule rendering it as its own body (\leanref{body}{name}), so the applied head and the body print alike
typed_info: the def name, its binders, value_expression; the display.json / layer entry for the head
occurrences: 10 of 141 lineup definitions; all-modules count in report
count_method: typed probe: _definitional_sides on every definition in the lineup modules' tables, lhs == rhs after removing \leanref
why: the card states body = body: the defined name never appears; a form prints the name with its binders (f(t, x) = ...)

trigger: species disj_left/disj_right (Or.inl / Or.inr)
typed_info: which disjunct, the proof of that disjunct
why: names which alternative is proved; when nothing is cited the disjunct's own proof is missing (R2), counted in "alternative holds." 514/161

phrase: Hence X, its first/second alternative holding
trigger: closer Or.inl/Or.inr constructor
typed_info: as above
why: as above

phrase: Both parts are shown; hence X / Both directions are shown; hence X
trigger: closer species conj / iff after printed parts
typed_info: the parts
why: the parts are printed above it

phrase: Both parts hold, so the claim holds.
trigger: And.intro closer with no cited premises
typed_info: the two component terms
why: neither part is cited or shown

trigger: closer head Iff.intro (_other_head_reading)
typed_info: the two implications
why: neither direction is cited or shown

trigger: Exists.intro closer with a typed witness
typed_info: the witness term
why: names the witness from the term

trigger: Subtype.mk, or Exists.intro with withheld / tautological witness
typed_info: the witness and the property proof
why: no witness and no reason

trigger: local proof head with nothing cited (3984); projection with no cited (3986); species witness (4074)
typed_info: the local fact / projected structure / witness
count_method: page: "Hence \(..\)." exactly; shared by several sites, split in the sample probe
why: no reason

trigger: species "sorry"
why: an honest gap already; "\texttt{sorry}" is Lean vocabulary but marks the gap

phrase: The remaining steps of this argument are not shown.
trigger: walk.exhausted under apm-paper policy
why: already a marked gap (not on any head page)

trigger: closer with step.name set to anything other than a tactic phrase (an arm's seg_phrase, or a name)
typed_info: the closing term
why: step.name is a source-text phrase or raw name, never a typed reason

trigger: a constant with no display rule
typed_info: the constant (a display rule would name it)
why: Rob's code; the render step removes it on the census pages, but it still reaches cards and conditions (render.py:3979 checks for it)

phrase: tactic name -> phrase: linear arithmetic, simplification, integer arithmetic, ring normalisation, positivity, function-property automation, decision procedure, ...
trigger: any site reading a tactic name (361-403, 1394, 3321)
typed_info: the tactic name only
occurrences: 1226 "— by <tactic>." (simplification 598, integer arithmetic 238, contradiction 134, linear arithmetic 53, ring normalisation 52, function-property automation 45, numeric normalisation 40, positivity 23, nonlinear 18, field simplification 17, decision procedure 5, continuity 3)
why: the table turns procedures into reasons; its uses are the sites above

phrase: lemma-keyed readings: "by linearity of the integral", "since the integrands agree almost everywhere", "by Lagrange's theorem", "as a composition of continuous functions"...
trigger: a row or closer whose lemma is a key in the data file
typed_info: the lemma name (key) and its instance
occurrences: e.g. 208 linearity of the integral; 69 Lagrange; 118 composition of continuous functions
why: the reading is keyed by the lemma actually used, so it names that lemma's content
